To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 3xTGAD mouse model of Alzheimer's disease has robust intraneuronic amyloid-β accumulation that is not free amyloid-β peptide, but instead is the full-length amyloid precursor protein.
the intraneural Aβ immunoreactivity detected in the 2xTg mice was not due to the presence of free Aβ peptides.
we found that the intracellular material that was reported to be Aβ in the 3Tg-AD mouse was not Aβ but rather APP, and that the accumulation of APP was independent of the generation of Aβ peptide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the amyloid precursor (APP) protein in the pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease (Alzheimer's & Dementia 2013).
the role of APP in AD
the development of a mouse model for Alzheimer's disease (3xTig-AD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the intraneural material in this model is APP, and not Aβ peptide, and therefore the 3x Tg-AD model does not support the idea that Aβ is the initiator of AD pathogenesis, but instead supports the idea that APP is the initiator of tau pathology.
intraneuronal amyloid β (Aβ) is not the culprit of tau pathology in the 3×Tg-AD mouse, as the authors suggest.
intraneuronal immunoreactivity in the 3×Tg-AD mouse is due to intraneuronal accumulation of APP and not due to free Aβ peptides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3xTG-AD mice have intracellular Aβ immunoreactivity that is not free Aβ peptides but rather is full-length APP and that the 3Tg-AD and 3xT-AD/BACE mice have similar levels of tau pathology.

the intraneuronally accumulated Aβ peptide in this mouse model of AD may be a result of the overexpression of APP, and that this intraneuronally deposited Aβ peptide is not the initiator of tau pathology in this model.

the 3xTG mouse model of Alzheimer's disease is a unique mouse model in that it has both Aβ and tau pathology and it is a model that is being used to understand the relationship of Aβ and tau in the pathogenesis of AD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intraneuronal amyloid-β peptide accumulation is not a feature of Alzheimer's disease ( AD ) pathology in 3xTG-AD mice.
intraneuronal amyloid-β is unlikely to be the initiator of Alzheimer's disease in 3xTransgenic-AD mice.
the 3x Tg-AD mouse is an interesting model for tauopathy and APP misprocessing but not for Aβ peptide generation and Aβ-mediated neurodegeneration.
